title: Transduction of a Concatenation
statement: Let $R,C$ be types, let $visit\colon R\times C\to R\times C$ be a local rule, let $s\in R$, and let $as,bs$ be finite words over $C$. Processing $as$ followed by $bs$ from state $s$ gives the same final state and rewritten word as first processing $as$ from $s$ and then processing $bs$ from the resulting state; the rewritten output is the concatenation of the two rewritten words.
hypotheses_covered: $visit$ is a function from $R\times C$ to $R\times C$
replaced:
Let $\mathit{visit} \colon R \times C \to R \times C$ be a local rule, $s$ an
initial control state, and $\mathit{as}$, $\mathit{bs}$ two words over $C$.
The finite-state transduction of the concatenation
$\mathit{as} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathit{bs}$ starting from $s$ is obtained by
transducing $\mathit{as}$ from $s$, then transducing $\mathit{bs}$ from the
resulting control state: the final state is that of the second transduction,
and the rewritten word is the concatenation of the two rewritten words.
